chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah raised it (narrated) and said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'Do not whisper to anyone in your gathering, and if you become angry, stand up, and do not pass judgment while you are angry.'
He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The tongue of the judge is behind his heart; if it is for him, he speaks, and if it is against him, he remains silent.'

key_terms.تَقْضِيَنَّ: To pass judgment or render a verdict
key_terms.تُسَارَّ: To whisper or speak secretly to someone
key_terms.شُرَيْح: Shurayh ibn al-Harith, a famous judge

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical rules for a judge's behavior and impartiality in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam Ali (AS) to the renowned judge Shuraih, establishes the psychological basis of judicial integrity by linking the tongue directly to the heart's state. It advises judges to withdraw when angry to prevent emotional bias and highlights the concept of 'self-restraint' (imsak) when personal interest conflicts with justice, a principle deeply valued in Shia jurisprudence for ensuring fair verdicts.
